\(R^2\) & r\_squared & Higher is better & Coefficient of determination. Higher values indicate that the fitted curve follows more of the observed response pattern. \\
Adjusted \(R^2\) & adjusted\_r\_squared & Higher is better & \(R^2\) adjusted for the number of fitted parameters. It can decrease when extra parameters do not improve the fit enough to justify the added complexity. \\
MSE & mse & Lower is better & Average squared difference between observed and fitted values. Lower values indicate smaller model errors, but the squared units can be harder to interpret directly. \\
RMSE & rmse & Lower is better & Typical model error in the same response units as the fitted data. Lower values indicate predictions closer to the observations. \\
MAE & mae & Lower is better & Average absolute model error in the same response units as the fitted data. Lower values indicate predictions closer to the observations. \\
NRMSE (mean) & mnrmse & Lower is better & RMSE divided by the response mean. Lower values indicate smaller error relative to the typical response magnitude. \\
NRMSE (std. dev.) & nrmse & Lower is better & RMSE divided by the response standard deviation. Lower values indicate smaller error relative to the amount of variation in the response. \\
AIC & aic & Lower is better & Akaike Information Criterion. AIC compares fitted models by considering both fit quality and the number of fitted parameters. Among comparable fitted models, a lower AIC value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that fits the data without unnecessary complexity. Absolute AIC values, including negative values, should not be interpreted as standalone quality grades. \\
AIC\textsubscript{c} & aicc & Lower is better & Corrected Akaike Information Criterion. AIC\textsubscript{c} is AIC with an added small-sample correction and is often preferred when the number of fitted observations is limited relative to the number of fitted parameters. See the user guide for additional information. Among comparable fitted models, a lower AIC\textsubscript{c} value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that balances fit quality and complexity; AIC\textsubscript{c} is undefined when there are too few observations relative to the number of parameters. \\
BIC & bic & Lower is better & Bayesian Information Criterion. BIC compares fitted models by considering both fit quality and the number of fitted parameters, usually applying a stronger penalty for extra parameters than AIC. Among comparable fitted models, a lower BIC value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that fits the data without unnecessary complexity. Absolute BIC values, including negative values, should not be interpreted as standalone quality grades. \\
